Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]` markers; investigate failures before moving on. On Windows a killed process settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker; treat a bare exit 1 after an interruption as a termination, not a command failure.

Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Use the glob tool — not shell find — to discover files by path pattern. A pattern with no "/" matches basenames at any depth, so "*" matches every file in the tree rather than its top level. Results are files only, never directories, and include hidden and ignored files: a result that fits comes back in modification-time order, while a larger one keeps the modification-time-ordered head.

Use the grep tool — not shell grep or rg — to search file contents. Use read on a matched file when you need surrounding context.

Use the web_search tool to discover current information on the web. The required queries array accepts 1–4 non-empty search queries; use a one-item array for a single search. Use goal tools for one long-running completion objective in the current session. create_goal may infer goal intent from a direct human request in any language; do not create a goal for routine single-turn work. After session resume or fork, an active goal is disarmed: when a human asks to continue or resume in any wording or language, use update_goal action resume to rearm it. Mark complete only when the objective is actually achieved. Mark blocked only after the same blocking condition persists for at least 3 consecutive goal rounds, and report that concrete condition in blocked_reason; difficulty, uncertainty, or useful remaining work is not blocked.

Use the workflow tool ONLY when the user explicitly asks for a workflow or for large multi-agent orchestration: you write a JavaScript script (the tool description documents the exact format) that fans work out across many subagents with phases and structured results. For one or two delegations, prefer plain subagent calls.

Use the ralph tool ONLY when the direct human explicitly asks for a Ralph loop or fresh-agent iterative execution. Each Ralph round starts a fresh child with no conversation seed and uses the shared workspace as durable memory. Completion and blockers are worker reports, not independent evaluation. Use same-session goal tools for ordinary long-running objectives, and plain subagents or workflows for bounded delegation and fan-out.

Use subagent in the background by default. Start independent delegations together in one assistant message and continue useful work while they run. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on that subagent's result. When a background run settles, the runtime sends you a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message.

Use subagent_fork in the background by default. Start independent delegations together in one assistant message and continue useful work while they run. tools.name: ask_user_question
tools.description: Ask the user a concise question when you need confirmation, a choice, or missing information before proceeding. Send one or more questions, each with a stable id that will be echoed in the answer.

id.description: Stable id for this question; echoed in the answer.

header.description: Optional short heading for the question, such as "Confirm" or "Choose Mode".

options.description: Optional choices to show the user. If you recommend one, put it first and append "(Recommended)" to that label.

description.description: One sentence explaining the tradeoff or impact.

multi_select.description: Whether the user may select more than one option. Defaults to false.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create one persisted same-session completion goal when the current direct human request is a long-running objective that should continue across autonomous goal rounds. You may infer that intent without requiring the user to say "create a goal". Do not use this for trivial single-turn work. Execution rejects non-human and subagent authority.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this file operation needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of an operation the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result returns the first 100 paths in modification-time order, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns the first 250 matches inline; a capped result reports where the complete match list was saved. Use read on a matched file for surrounding context.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Request cancellation of a background agent's current turn by its agent id. The target may be your direct child or a deeper agent created under you. Only the current turn stops: messages already queued for the agent stay parked until a later send_message, agents it started keep running, and the agent itself stays available for follow-ups. This call returns as soon as the stop request is accepted, so the target may keep running briefly; interrupting an agent that already finished is an accepted no-op.

agent_id.description: The agent id of the running agent to interrupt.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List your continuable background subagents by durable id and label. Use it to recall which ones you started, not to poll for completion — you are told when one finishes. Status comes from the live registry: running means the agent is working right now, idle means it is loaded but between turns (it may be waiting on agents it started), and ready means it exists only in storage — resumable, not terminal, and not a result waiting to be collected; a `send_message` steers a running child at its nearest step boundary or starts a turn for an idle or ready child, and a direct child remains a `send_message` candidate in every status. The snapshot is not a delivery promise — `send_message` performs the authoritative check and may still fail. Children that could not be read are reported as diagnostics instead of being silently dropped. Scope `descendants` walks the whole tree below you in stable pre-order, annotating each entry with its durable direct-parent session id and depth. You may use `send_message` only for depth-1 entries; deeper entries are candidates for `interrupt_agent` only.

scope.description: children (default) lists direct children only; descendants walks the complete tree below you.

tools.description: Discover LLM routes for subagents without changing the current Agent. Call with no arguments to list registered providers, with `provider` to list its advertised models, or with `provider` and `model` to inspect that exact model and its reasoning efforts. Catalog membership is advisory: an adapter may accept an unlisted model id. Use the returned ids with a delegation tool's `provider`, `model`, and `reasoning_effort` fields.

provider.description: Registered LLM provider id. Omit to list providers.

model.description: Exact model id to inspect. Requires provider; omit to list that provider's advertised models.

tools.name: present

Mentioning its path in your reply does not replace this call. The files must already exist. The user opens the current source files; their contents are not copied or preserved.

path.description: Path of an existing regular file. Relative paths use the Session working directory.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$env:DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output. Attempting a command the sandbox may deny is safe and expected: run it and read the marker rather than assuming the denial. When a command is denied and a wider mode would let it succeed, escalate immediately in the same turn — the one sanctioned exception to a denial: retry the exact same command once with `sandbox_permissions` (the narrowest wider mode that suffices) plus a one-sentence `justification`. Do not detour through chat to ask permission first — the approval prompt raised by that retry is how the user consents. If the session states approval prompts are disabled, there is no exception: a denial is final — do not set `sandbox_permissions`. Never escalate speculatively: ground the request in a real denial — normally the one this command just hit; escalating up front is fine only when this session already denied the same access. A rejected escalation is final for that command — stop and explain, never work around it — but it does not forbid attempting or escalating other commands later.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "Get-Process" → "List running processes".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

tools.name: ralph
tools.description: Run a foreground fresh-agent Ralph loop toward one immutable objective. Use only when the direct human explicitly asks for Ralph or fresh-agent iteration. Each round opens a new child with no parent conversation or prior child session; the shared workspace is long-term memory, and only a bounded structured report crosses rounds. The call returns when a worker reports completion or a concrete blocker, or at the round limit. Ordinary long-running same-session work belongs to goal tools.

objective.description: The immutable completion objective for every fresh Ralph round.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. A path without a file extension is accepted; the format is detected from the file content, so normalized attachment paths can be passed directly without copying or renaming. Harness validates and downscales large supported images before the next model request, so use this tool directly instead of installing image libraries or creating thumbnails merely to inspect an image. Independent files may be read concurrently in small batches. Requires the current model to accept image input.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to a direct continuable child by its agent id. If you are a resident continuable child, you may also target your direct parent. If the target is still working, the message steers its nearest step; if it is idle, the message starts a turn. This call returns no answer from the agent — only confirmation that the message was delivered. A failure means the message was NOT delivered.

agent_id.description: The agent id of your direct continuable child, or your direct parent when you are a resident continuable child.

message.description: The message to deliver to the agent.

tools.name: subagent
tools.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. Give it a complete, standalone prompt: it does not see this conversation. This tool runs in the background by default, immediately returns a durable subagent id, and keeps the child conversation available for later turns. When that run settles, the runtime sends the parent a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message; `send_message` steers the child's nearest step while it is running and starts a turn while it is idle. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on receiving the result. Child LLM selection is optional. Omit `provider`, `model`, and `reasoning_effort` to use configured child defaults and inherit compatible missing values from the parent Agent. Supply `provider` and `model` together after using `list_subagent_models` to inspect advertised routes and efforts. Changing the effective route without naming an effort uses the selected model's default effort.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs.

provider.description: LLM provider route for the child. Supply together with model; omit both to use configured child defaults or inherit the parent route.

model.description: Model id interpreted by provider. Supply together with provider; omit both to use configured child defaults or inherit the parent route.

reasoning_effort.description: Adapter-owned reasoning effort for the effective child route. Omit to inherit a compatible configured/parent effort or use a newly selected model's default.

run_in_background.description: Whether to run in the background and return a durable subagent id immediately. Defaults to true. Set false to wait for the result when your next action depends on it.

tools.name: subagent_fork
tools.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool runs in the background by default, immediately returns a durable subagent id, and keeps the child conversation available for later turns. When that run settles, the runtime sends the parent a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message; `send_message` steers the child's nearest step while it is running and starts a turn while it is idle. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on receiving the result.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The task for the subagent. It already sees this conversation's completed turns, so build on them freely and state only what is new.

run_in_background.description: Whether to run in the background and return a durable subagent id immediately. Defaults to true. Set false to wait for the result when your next action depends on it.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

The workflow's identity rides the `meta` parameter as JSON: required `name` (short kebab-case) and `description` strings, optional `whenToUse` string and `phases` array (`{title, detail?, provider?, model?}`). The `script` parameter is the plain JavaScript body ONLY (NOT TypeScript, and NO `export const meta` statement — meta is a parameter, not code), running with top-level await; end with `return <value>` — the value must be JSON-serializable and is this tool's result.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf — no pattern/format/numeric bounds) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides (either may be provided alone). Anything else (`effort`/`isolation`/`agentType`) is rejected loudly.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. An ordinary stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) throw errors that ALWAYS kill the script — they never dissolve into a per-item `null`.

Constraints: concurrency and total-agent caps apply; no filesystem, network, timers, or Node.js APIs are provided — the agents do the work, the script only coordinates them. The run executes in the foreground: this call returns when the whole script finishes.

script.description: The plain-JS workflow script body (top-level await allowed; NO `export const meta` statement; end with `return <json-value>`).

meta.description: The workflow identity block (plain JSON — never code).

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

# Agent notes — Venue Vue

Venue Vue is an offline-first Point of Sale and event-management app (React 19,

  amending, or squashing commits that are already pushed.

  `npm run build` must pass before pushing.

  not rename them without a migration.

ship to production as-is).

1: /**
2:  * IndexedDB-based offline-first storage layer.
3:  *
4:  * Strategy:
5:  *  1. Read/write locally first (IndexedDB)
6:  *  2. Queue offline mutations so they can be synced later
7:  *  3. Sync queued changes to the backend when back online
8:  *  4. Prevent duplicate synchronization using a "syncedAt" timestamp
9:  */
10: 
11: const DB_NAME = "venue-vue-offline";
12: const DB_VERSION = 1;
13: export const STORE_NAME = "mutations";
14: 
15: /** Keys in the store that are not queued mutations. */
16: function isReservedKey(id: string) {
17:   return id === "currentUser" || id === "offlineSession" || id.startsWith("auth:");
18: }
19: 
20: function getIndexedDB(): IDBFactory | undefined {
21:   if (typeof window === "undefined") return undefined;
22:   return window.indexedDB;
23: }
24: 
25: export function openOfflineDB(): Promise<IDBDatabase> {
26:   return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
27:     const idb = getIndexedDB();
28:     if (!idb) {
29:       reject(new Error("IndexedDB not supported"));
30:       return;
31:     }
32:     const request = idb.open(DB_NAME, DB_VERSION);
33:     request.onupgradeneeded = () => {
34:       const db = request.result;
35:       if (!db.objectStoreNames.contains(STORE_NAME)) {
36:         db.createObjectStore(STORE_NAME);
37:       }
38:     };
39:     request.onsuccess = () => resolve(request.result);
40:     request.onerror = () => reject(request.error ?? new Error("IndexedDB open failed"));
41:     request.onblocked = () => reject(new Error("IndexedDB upgrade blocked"));
42:   });
43: }
44: 
45: export function promisifyRequest<T>(request: IDBRequest<T>): Promise<T> {
46:   return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
47:     request.onsuccess = () => resolve(request.result);
48:     request.onerror = () => reject(request.error ?? new Error("IndexedDB request failed"));
49:   });
50: }
51: 
52: export function txDone(tx: IDBTransaction): Promise<void> {
53:   return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
54:     tx.oncomplete = () => resolve();
55:     tx.onabort = () => reject(tx.error ?? new Error("IndexedDB transaction aborted"));
56:     tx.onerror = () => reject(tx.error ?? new Error("IndexedDB transaction failed"));
57:   });
58: }
59: 
60: export interface MutationEntry {
61:   id: string;
62:   type: "insert" | "update" | "delete";
63:   table: string;
64:   data?: unknown;
65:   where?: unknown;
66:   createdAt: number;
67:   syncedAt?: number;
68: }
69: 
70: export interface LocalUser {
71:   email: string;
72:   role?: string;
73:   userId: string;
74: }
75: 
76: interface UserEntry {
77:   id: string;
78:   data: LocalUser;
79:   createdAt: number;
80:   syncedAt: number;
81: }
82: 
83: /** Store a mutation entry for offline sync. */
84: export async function queueMutation(
85:   type: MutationEntry["type"],
86:   table: string,
87:   data?: unknown,
88:   where?: unknown,
89: ): Promise<string> {
90:   const id = `${table}:${type}:${Date.now()}:${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2)}`;
91:   const entry: MutationEntry = { id, type, table, data, where, createdAt: Date.now() };
92: 
93:   const db = await openOfflineDB();
94:   const tx = db.transaction(STORE_NAME, "readwrite");
95:   tx.objectStore(STORE_NAME).put(entry, entry.id);
96:   await txDone(tx);
97:   return id;
98: }
99: 
100: /** Get all pending (unsynced) mutations. */
101: export async function getPendingMutations(): Promise<MutationEntry[]> {
102:   const db = await openOfflineDB();
103:   const tx = db.transaction(STORE_NAME, "readonly");
104:   const all = await promisifyRequest(tx.objectStore(STORE_NAME).getAll());
105:   return (all as MutationEntry[]).filter(
106:     (entry) => entry && entry.id && !isReservedKey(entry.id) && entry.syncedAt === undefined,
107:   );
108: }
109: 
110: /** Mark a mutation as synced by its id. */
111: export async function markSynced(mutationId: string): Promise<void> {
112:   const db = await openOfflineDB();
113:   const tx = db.transaction(STORE_NAME, "readwrite");
114:   const store = tx.objectStore(STORE_NAME);
115:   const entry = (await promisifyRequest(store.get(mutationId))) as MutationEntry | undefined;
116:   if (entry) {
117:     entry.syncedAt = Date.now();
118:     store.put(entry, entry.id);
119:   }
120:   await txDone(tx);
121: }
122: 
123: /** Clear all synced mutations, keeping only pending ones. */
124: export async function clearSyncedMutations(): Promise<void> {
125:   const db = await openOfflineDB();
126:   const tx = db.transaction(STORE_NAME, "readwrite");
127:   const store = tx.objectStore(STORE_NAME);
128:   const all = (await promisifyRequest(store.getAll())) as MutationEntry[];
129:   for (const entry of all) {
130:     if (entry && entry.id && !isReservedKey(entry.id) && entry.syncedAt !== undefined) {
131:       store.delete(entry.id);
132:     }
133:   }
134:   await txDone(tx);
135: }
136: 
137: /** Read the cached signed-in user, if one was stored. */
138: export async function getUserFromLocal(): Promise<{ user: LocalUser } | null> {
139:   if (typeof window === "undefined") return null;
140:   try {
141:     const db = await openOfflineDB();
142:     const tx = db.transaction(STORE_NAME, "readonly");
143:     const entry = (await promisifyRequest(tx.objectStore(STORE_NAME).get("currentUser"))) as
144:       | UserEntry
145:       | undefined;
146:     if (entry?.data) return { user: entry.data };
147:   } catch {
148:     // IndexedDB unavailable — fall through to the network path.
149:   }
150:   return null;
151: }
152: 
153: /** Cache the signed-in user for offline use. */
154: export async function storeUserLocally(userData: LocalUser): Promise<void> {
155:   if (typeof window === "undefined") return;
156:   try {
157:     const db = await openOfflineDB();
158:     const tx = db.transaction(STORE_NAME, "readwrite");
159:     const entry: UserEntry = {
160:       id: "currentUser",
161:       data: userData,
162:       createdAt: Date.now(),
163:       syncedAt: Date.now(),
164:     };
165:     tx.objectStore(STORE_NAME).put(entry, entry.id);
166:     await txDone(tx);
167:   } catch {
168:     // Non-fatal: offline caching is best effort.
169:   }
170: }
171: 
172: export default {
173:   queueMutation,
174:   getPendingMutations,
175:   markSynced,
176:   clearSyncedMutations,
177:   getUserFromLocal,
178:   storeUserLocally,
179: };

1: import { useEffect } from "react";
2: import { useQueryClient } from "@tanstack/react-query";
3: import { supabase } from "@/integrations/supabase/client";
4: import {
5:   clearSyncedMutations,
6:   getPendingMutations,
7:   markSynced,
8: } from "@/lib/offline-storage";
9: 
10: /**
11:  * Replays anything queued while offline as soon as the connection returns.
12:  */
13: export function useOfflineSync() {
14:   const queryClient = useQueryClient();
15: 
16:   useEffect(() => {
17:     let running = false;
18: 
19:     async function sync() {
20:       if (running || typeof navigator === "undefined" || !navigator.onLine) return;
21:       running = true;
22:       try {
23:         const pending = await getPendingMutations();
24:         for (const mutation of pending) {
25:           const table = supabase.from(mutation.table as never);
26:           try {
27:             if (mutation.type === "insert") {
28:               await table.insert(mutation.data as never);
29:             } else if (mutation.type === "update") {
30:               await table.update(mutation.data as never).match(mutation.where as never);
31:             } else if (mutation.type === "delete") {
32:               await table.delete().match(mutation.where as never);
33:             }
34:             await markSynced(mutation.id);
35:           } catch {
36:             // Leave it queued for the next reconnect.
37:           }
38:         }
39:         await clearSyncedMutations();
40:         if (pending.length > 0) await queryClient.invalidateQueries();
41:       } catch {
42:         // IndexedDB unavailable — nothing to sync.
43:       } finally {
44:         running = false;
45:       }
46:     }
47: 
48:     void sync();
49:     window.addEventListener("online", sync);
50:     return () => window.removeEventListener("online", sync);
51:   }, [queryClient]);
52: }

1: /**
2:  * Offline credential vault + local session.
3:  *
4:  * Two layers, both device-local:
5:  *
6:  *  1. `venuevue_session` in localStorage — the lightweight session the app
7:  *     treats as "signed in" on load. Written by {@link signInLocally} and by a
8:  *     successful online sign-in, so a page refresh (F5) survives without any
9:  *     network round-trip.
10:  *  2. A PBKDF2 credential vault in IndexedDB — after a successful ONLINE
11:  *     sign-in we store the user's identity plus a salted hash of their
12:  *     password. With no connection the login form verifies the typed password
13:  *     against that hash, so a returning user can still open the register.
14:  *
15:  * A built-in demo account (admin@venuevue.local / PIN 1234) is always accepted
16:  * locally, so the register works on a brand-new device with no backend at all.
17:  *
18:  * Only a salted hash is stored — never the plaintext password.
19:  */
20: 
21: import {
22:   openOfflineDB,
23:   promisifyRequest,
24:   txDone,
25:   STORE_NAME,
26:   storeUserLocally,
27: } from "./offline-storage";
28: 
29: const PBKDF2_ITERATIONS = 150_000;
30: const SESSION_KEY = "offlineSession";
31: const SESSION_FLAG = "venue-vue-offline-session";
32: 
33: /** localStorage key holding the device session. */
34: export const SESSION_STORAGE_KEY = "venuevue_session";
35: 
36: /** Marker token for sessions that were created without the backend. */
37: export const OFFLINE_DEMO_TOKEN = "offline-demo-token";
38: 
39: /** Built-in local account — always valid on this device, network or not. */
40: export const LOCAL_DEMO_EMAIL = "admin@venuevue.local";
41: export const LOCAL_DEMO_PIN = "1234";
42: export const LOCAL_DEMO_ROLE = "admin";
43: export const LOCAL_DEMO_USER_ID = "demo-local-admin";
44: 
45: /** Shape of the session object kept under `venuevue_session`. */
46: export interface LocalSession {
47:   user: { email: string; role: string };
48:   token: string;
49: }
50: 
51: export interface OfflineAuthRecord {
52:   id: string;
53:   email: string;
54:   userId: string;
55:   role: string;
56:   salt: string;
57:   passwordHash: string;
58:   cachedAt: number;
59: }
60: 
61: export interface OfflineSession {
62:   email: string;
63:   userId: string;
64:   role: string;
65:   startedAt: number;
66: }
67: 
68: function authKey(email: string) {
69:   return `auth:${email.trim().toLowerCase()}`;
70: }
71: 
72: function toHex(buffer: ArrayBuffer) {
73:   return Array.from(new Uint8Array(buffer))
74:     .map((b) => b.toString(16).padStart(2, "0"))
75:     .join("");
76: }
77: 
78: function fromHex(hex: string) {
79:   const bytes = new Uint8Array(hex.length / 2);
80:   for (let i = 0; i < bytes.length; i += 1) {
81:     bytes[i] = parseInt(hex.slice(i * 2, i * 2 + 2), 16);
82:   }
83:   return bytes;
84: }
85: 
86: async function hashPassword(password: string, salt: Uint8Array): Promise<string> {
87:   const keyMaterial = await crypto.subtle.importKey(
88:     "raw",
89:     new TextEncoder().encode(password),
90:     "PBKDF2",
91:     false,
92:     ["deriveBits"],
93:   );
94:   const bits = await crypto.subtle.deriveBits(
95:     {
96:       name: "PBKDF2",
97:       // BufferSource copy keeps TS happy across lib targets
98:       salt: salt.slice(),
99:       iterations: PBKDF2_ITERATIONS,
100:       hash: "SHA-256",
101:     },
102:     keyMaterial,
103:     256,
104:   );
105:   return toHex(bits);
106: }
107: 
108: function timingSafeEqual(a: string, b: string) {
109:   if (a.length !== b.length) return false;
110:   let diff = 0;
111:   for (let i = 0; i < a.length; i += 1) diff |= a.charCodeAt(i) ^ b.charCodeAt(i);
112:   return diff === 0;
113: }
114: 
115: const NETWORK_ERROR_PATTERN =
116:   /failed to fetch|load failed|networkerror|network error|err_network|fetch failed|network request failed|connection.*(refused|reset|closed)|timed? ?out|offline/i;
117: 
118: /**
119:  * True when a thrown value (or Supabase error) means "the backend could not be
120:  * reached" rather than "the backend said no".
121:  *
122:  * supabase-js reports a dead `fetch` as an `AuthRetryableFetchError` with
123:  * status 0 and the browser message (`Failed to fetch` on Chromium,
124:  * `Load failed` on Safari/iOS, `NetworkError when attempting to fetch
125:  * resource.` on Firefox); gateway/Cloudflare errors come back with a 5xx
126:  * status. Anything else is a real answer from the server and must not be
127:  * swallowed.
128:  */
129: export function isNetworkError(error: unknown): boolean {
130:   if (error === null || error === undefined) return false;
131:   if (typeof error === "string") return NETWORK_ERROR_PATTERN.test(error);
132: 
133:   const { name, message, status } = error as {
134:     name?: unknown;
135:     message?: unknown;
136:     status?: unknown;
137:   };
138:   if (name === "AuthRetryableFetchError" || name === "AbortError") return true;
139:   if (status === 0) return true;
140: 
141:   return NETWORK_ERROR_PATTERN.test(
142:     `${typeof name === "string" ? name : ""} ${typeof message === "string" ? message : ""}`,
143:   );
144: }
145: 
146: function isLocalSession(value: unknown): value is LocalSession {
147:   if (typeof value !== "object" || value === null) return false;
148:   const { user, token } = value as { user?: unknown; token?: unknown };
149:   if (typeof token !== "string" || token.length === 0) return false;
150:   if (typeof user !== "object" || user === null) return false;
151:   const { email, role } = user as { email?: unknown; role?: unknown };
152:   return typeof email === "string" && email.length > 0 && typeof role === "string" && role.length > 0;
153: }
154: 
155: /** Build the canonical device session object. */
156: export function createLocalSession(
157:   email: string,
158:   role: string,
159:   token: string = OFFLINE_DEMO_TOKEN,
160: ): LocalSession {
161:   return { user: { email: email.trim(), role }, token };
162: }
163: 
164: /**
165:  * Persist the device session. The `token` is a local marker only — the real
166:  * Supabase JWT stays in Supabase's own auth storage, never duplicated here.
167:  */
168: export function saveLocalSession(session: LocalSession): void {
169:   if (typeof window === "undefined") return;
170:   try {
171:     window.localStorage.setItem(SESSION_STORAGE_KEY, JSON.stringify(session));
172:   } catch {
173:     // Private mode / storage disabled — the app still works for this tab.
174:   }
175: }
176: 
177: /** Read the device session, if one was stored and is still well-formed. */
178: export function getLocalSession(): LocalSession | null {
179:   if (typeof window === "undefined") return null;
180:   try {
181:     const raw = window.localStorage.getItem(SESSION_STORAGE_KEY);
182:     if (!raw) return null;
183:     const parsed = JSON.parse(raw) as unknown;
184:     return isLocalSession(parsed) ? parsed : null;
185:   } catch {
186:     return null;
187:   }
188: }
189: 
190: /** Drop the device session (the credential vault is kept intact). */
191: export function clearLocalSession(): void {
192:   if (typeof window === "undefined") return;
193:   try {
194:     window.localStorage.removeItem(SESSION_STORAGE_KEY);
195:   } catch {
196:     /* ignore */
197:   }
198: }
199: 
200: /**
201:  * Refresh survival: return the session stored on this device, rehydrating the
202:  * localStorage copy from the IndexedDB vault when only the latter survived.
203:  */
204: export async function restoreLocalSession(): Promise<LocalSession | null> {
205:   const stored = getLocalSession();
206:   if (stored) return stored;
207: 
208:   const vaultSession = await getOfflineSession();
209:   if (!vaultSession) return null;
210: 
211:   const session = createLocalSession(vaultSession.email, vaultSession.role);
212:   saveLocalSession(session);
213:   return session;
214: }
215: 
216: function matchesLocalDemoAccount(email: string, credential: string): boolean {
217:   return (
218:     email.trim().toLowerCase() === LOCAL_DEMO_EMAIL && timingSafeEqual(credential, LOCAL_DEMO_PIN)
219:   );
220: }
221: 
222: /**
223:  * Sign in without the backend: the built-in demo account, or any account whose
224:  * credentials were cached on this device after a previous online sign-in.
225:  *
226:  * On success the device session is persisted (`venuevue_session`), the offline
227:  * session marker is raised and the user is cached for the signed-in shell.
228:  */
229: export async function signInLocally(
230:   email: string,
231:   credential: string,
232: ): Promise<LocalSession | null> {
233:   let session: LocalSession | null = null;
234:   let userId = "";
235: 
236:   if (matchesLocalDemoAccount(email, credential)) {
237:     session = createLocalSession(LOCAL_DEMO_EMAIL, LOCAL_DEMO_ROLE);
238:     userId = LOCAL_DEMO_USER_ID;
239:   } else {
240:     const vault = await verifyOfflineCredentials(email.trim(), credential);
241:     if (vault) {
242:       session = createLocalSession(vault.email, vault.role);
243:       userId = vault.userId || vault.email;
244:     }
245:   }
246: 
247:   if (!session) return null;
248: 
249:   saveLocalSession(session);
250:   await startOfflineSession({
251:     email: session.user.email,
252:     userId,
253:     role: session.user.role,
254:     startedAt: Date.now(),
255:   });
256:   await storeUserLocally({
257:     email: session.user.email,
258:     role: session.user.role,
259:     userId,
260:   });
261: 
262:   return session;
263: }
264: 
265: /** Remember these credentials so the user can sign in again with no network. */
266: export async function cacheCredentialsForOffline(params: {
267:   email: string;
268:   password: string;
269:   userId: string;
270:   role: string;
271: }): Promise<void> {
272:   if (typeof window === "undefined" || !window.crypto?.subtle) return;
273:   try {
274:     const salt = crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(16));
275:     const passwordHash = await hashPassword(params.password, salt);
276:     const record: OfflineAuthRecord = {
277:       id: authKey(params.email),
278:       email: params.email.trim(),
279:       userId: params.userId,
280:       role: params.role,
281:       salt: toHex(salt.buffer),
282:       passwordHash,
283:       cachedAt: Date.now(),
284:     };
285:     const db = await openOfflineDB();

1: <?php
2: /**
3:  * VenueVue Sync Backend
4:  * Handles incoming JSON order payloads from Flutter POS clients
5:  * Uses prepared statements to prevent SQL injection
6:  * Offline-first compatible: supports batch and individual sync
7:  */
8: 
9: // Configuration - adjust for your XAMPP/MySQL setup
10: define('DB_HOST', 'localhost');
11: define('DB_NAME', 'venuevue_db');
12: define('DB_USER', 'root');
13: define('DB_PASS', '');
14: define('CHARSET', 'utf8mb4');
15: 
16: // DSN for PDO connection
17: $dsn = "mysql:host=" . DB_HOST . ";dbname=" . DB_NAME . ";charset=" . CHARSET;
18: $options = [
19:     PDO::ATTR_ERRMODE            => PDO::ERRMODE_EXCEPTION,
20:     PDO::ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES   => false,
21:     PDO::ATTR_DEFAULT_FETCH_MODE => PDO::FETCH_ASSOC,
22: ];
23: 
24: try {
25:     $pdo = new PDO($dsn, DB_USER, DB_PASS, $options);
26: } catch (\PDOException $e) {
27:     // In production, log to file instead of displaying
28:     http_response_code(500);
29:     die(json_encode([
30:         'success' => false,
31:         'error' => 'Database connection failed',
32:         'message' => $e->getMessage()
33:     ]));
34: }
35: 
36: // Set error handling for JSON errors
37: header('Content-Type: application/json');
38: header('Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *');
39: header('Access-Control-Allow-Methods: POST, OPTIONS');
40: header('Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type, X-Requested-With');
41: 
42: // Handle OPTIONS preflight for CORS
43: if ($_SERVER['REQUEST_METHOD'] === 'OPTIONS') {
44:     http_response_code(200);
45:     exit();
46: }
47: 
48: // Ensure POST method
49: if ($_SERVER['REQUEST_METHOD'] !== 'POST') {
50:     http_response_code(405);
51:     die(json_encode([
52:         'success' => false,
53:         'error' => 'Method not allowed',
54:         'message' => 'POST method required'
55:     ]));
56: }
57: 
58: // Decode incoming JSON payload
59: $input = json_decode(file_get_contents('php://input'), true);
60: 
61: if ($input === null) {
62:     http_response_code(400);
63:     die(json_encode([
64:         'success' => false,
65:         'error' => 'Invalid JSON',
66:         'message' => 'Unable to decode request body'
67:     ]));
68: }
69: 
70: // Validate required fields
71: if (empty($input['order']) || !is_array($input['order'])) {
72:     http_response_code(400);
73:     die(json_encode([
74:         'success' => false,
75:         'error' => 'Missing order data',
76:         'message' => 'JSON payload must contain "order" array'
77:     ]));
78: }
79: 
80: // Start transaction for atomicity
81: try {
82:     $pdo->beginTransaction();
83: 
84:     // 1. Insert order header
85:     $order = $input['order'];
86:     
87:     // Validate order required fields
88:     $requiredOrderFields = ['user_id', 'status', 'payment_method', 'items'];
89:     foreach ($requiredOrderFields as $field) {
90:         if (empty($order[$field])) {
91:             throw new \Exception("Missing required order field: $field");
92:         }
93:     }
94: 
95:     $stmt = $pdo->prepare(
96:         "INSERT INTO orders (user_id, status, payment_method, total_amount, cash_tendered, change_due)
97:          VALUES (:user_id, :status, :payment_method, :total_amount, :cash_tendered, :change_due)"
98:     );
99: 
100:     $stmt->execute([
101:         ':user_id' => (int)$order['user_id'],
102:         ':status' => $order['status'],
103:         ':payment_method' => $order['payment_method'],
104:         ':total_amount' => floatval($order['total_amount'] ?? 0.00),
105:         ':cash_tendered' => floatval($order['cash_tendered'] ?? 0.00),
106:         ':change_due' => floatval($order['change_due'] ?? 0.00)
107:     ]);
108: 
109:     $orderId = $pdo->lastInsertId();
110: 
111:     // 2. Insert order items
112:     $totalAmount = 0.00;
113: 
114:     foreach ($order['items'] as $item) {
115:         $requiredItemFields = ['product_id', 'quantity'];
116:         foreach ($requiredItemFields as $field) {
117:             if (empty($item[$field])) {
118:                 throw new \Exception("Missing required item field: $field");
119:             }
120:         }
121: 
122:         // Get product base price for total calculation
123:         $productStmt = $pdo->prepare(
124:             "SELECT base_price, is_active FROM products WHERE product_id = :product_id"
125:         );
126:         $productStmt->execute([':product_id' => (int)$item['product_id']]);
127:         $product = $productStmt->fetch();
128: 
129:         if (!$product || !$product['is_active']) {
130:             throw new \Exception("Product not found or inactive: {$item['product_id']}");
131:         }
132: 
133:         $unitPrice = floatval($product['base_price']);
134:         $quantity = (int)$item['quantity'];
135:         $itemTotal = $unitPrice * $quantity;
136:         $totalAmount += $itemTotal;
137: 
138:         // Insert order item
139:         $itemStmt = $pdo->prepare(
140:             "INSERT INTO order_items (order_id, product_id, quantity, unit_price, total_price)
141:              VALUES (:order_id, :product_id, :quantity, :unit_price, :item_total)"
142:         );
143: 
144:         $itemStmt->execute([
145:             ':order_id' => $orderId,
146:             ':product_id' => (int)$item['product_id'],
147:             ':quantity' => $quantity,
148:             ':unit_price' => $unitPrice,
149:             ':item_total' => $itemTotal
150:         ]);
151:     }
152: 
153:     // 3. Update order total amount
154:     $updateStmt = $pdo->prepare(
155:         "UPDATE orders SET total_amount = :total_amount WHERE order_id = :order_id"
156:     );
157:     $updateStmt->execute([
158:         ':total_amount' => $totalAmount,
159:         ':order_id' => $orderId
160:     ]);
161: 
162:     // 4. Recipe-based inventory deduction (Phase 1 foundation)
163:     // For each order item, deduct recipe ingredients from stock
164:     $deductionStmt = $pdo->prepare(
165:         "SELECT ri.ingredient_id, ri.quantity_required, i.current_quantity, i.safety_stock
166:          FROM recipe_items ri
167:          JOIN ingredients i ON ri.ingredient_id = i.ingredient_id
168:          WHERE ri.product_id = :product_id"
169:     );
170: 
171:     foreach ($order['items'] as $item) {
172:         $productId = (int)$item['product_id'];
173:         $quantity = (int)$item['quantity'];
174: 
175:         $deductionStmt->execute([':product_id' => $productId]);
176:         $recipes = $deductionStmt->fetchAll();
177: 
178:         foreach ($recipes as $recipe) {
179:             $ingredientId = $recipe['ingredient_id'];
180:             $recipeQty = floatval($recipe['quantity_required']);
181:             $requiredTotal = $recipeQty * $quantity;
182: 
183:             // Check stock sufficiency
184:             $currentQty = floatval($recipe['current_quantity']);
185:             if ($currentQty < $requiredTotal) {
186:                 throw new \Exception(
187:                     "Insufficient stock for ingredient {$recipe['ingredient_id']}: " .
188:                     "required {$requiredTotal}{$recipe['unit']}, available {$currentQty}{$recipe['unit']}"
189:                 );
190:             }
191: 
192:             // Deduct from inventory

7: /// {@category Sync Service}
8: /// Provides offline-first synchronization between local SQLite database
9: /// and remote XAMPP PHP server over local Wi-Fi hotspot.
10: ///
11: /// This service handles:
12: /// - Checking for un-synced local orders
13: /// - Sending order payloads via HTTP POST to the backend API
14: /// - Marking orders as synced in local storage after successful transmission
15: /// - Graceful error handling with retry support
16: class SyncService {
17:   /// The base URL for the VenueVue PHP API sync endpoint.
18:   /// Adjust this for your XAMPP server IP address.
19:   static const String _syncEndpoint = 'http://192.168.137.1/venuevue_api/sync.php';

21:   /// Prepares an [OrderModel] into a JSON map suitable for transmission
22:   /// to the backend [sync.php] endpoint.
23:   ///
24:   /// The returned map contains all necessary fields for the PHP backend
25:   /// to insert the order, including order header data and associated items.
26:   ///
27:   /// @param order The local order model to serialize.
28:   /// @returns A JSON-compatible map ready for encoding.
29:   static Map<String, dynamic> prepareOrderData(OrderModel order) {
30:     return {
31:       'order_id': order.orderId,
32:       'user_id': order.userId,
33:       'status': order.status,
34:       'payment_method': order.paymentMethod,
35:       'total_amount': order.totalAmount,
36:       'cash_tendered': order.cashTendered,
37:       'change_due': order.changeDue,
38:       'created_at': order.createdAt.toIso8601String(),
39:       'closed_at': order.closedAt?.toIso8601String(),
40:       'synced': order.synced,
41:     };
42:   }

44:   /// Sends a single order to the sync endpoint and returns whether it was successful.
45:   ///
46:   /// The order data is serialized to JSON and posted to [_syncEndpoint]
47:   /// using the `application/json` content type.
48:   ///
49:   /// On success (HTTP 2xx with `success: true` in response body), returns `true`.
50:   /// On failure (network error, server error, or invalid response), returns `false`.
51:   ///
52:   /// @param order The order to sync to the server.
53:   /// @returns `true` if the order was successfully synced, `false` otherwise.
54:   static Future<bool> syncOrder(OrderModel order) async {
55:     final Uri url = Uri.parse(_syncEndpoint);
56: 
57:     final Map<String, dynamic> orderData = prepareOrderData(order);
58: 
59:     try {
60:       final http.Response response = await http.post(
61:         url,
62:         headers: {'Content-Type': 'application/json'},
63:         body: json.encode(orderData),
64:       );
65: 
66:       // Check for successful HTTP response (2xx status code)
67:       if (response.statusCode >= 200 && response.statusCode < 300) {
68:         final Map<String, dynamic> responseBody = json.decode(response.body);
69:         return responseBody['success'] == true;
70:       }
71: 
72:       return false;
73:     } catch (e) {
74:       // Network errors, timeout, or other exceptions
75:       return false;
76:     }
77:   }

79:   /// Synchronizes all unsynced orders from local SQLite to the remote server.

81:   /// Iterates through all unsynced orders found via [DatabaseHelper.getUnsyncedOrders],
82:   /// attempts to sync each one using [syncOrder], and marks successfully synced

**🔴 THE CRITICAL DEFECT — neither client's payload can be accepted by `sync.php`.**

- **A** (`sync_service.dart:14-19`) posts the **raw SQLite row**: `body: jsonEncode(order)` where `order` is the `local_orders` map `{id, order_uuid, total_amount, cash_tendered, change_due, created_at, is_synced}`.
- **B** (`sync_service.dart:29-42, 60-64`) posts `prepareOrderData(order)` — a **flat** map `{order_id, user_id, status, payment_method, total_amount, cash_tendered, change_due, created_at, closed_at, synced}`.
- **`sync.php:71`** requires a nested envelope: `if (empty($input['order']) || !is_array($input['order']))` → **HTTP 400 "Missing order data"**.
- **`sync.php:88`** additionally requires `['user_id','status','payment_method','items']` inside `$order`, and `:114` iterates `$order['items']`. **Neither client ever sends an `items` array** — A never reads `local_order_items` in its sync path, and B's `prepareOrderData` has no `items` key. So even if wrapped correctly, the request would throw `Missing required order field: items` → HTTP 500.
- **Net effect: 100% of orders fail to sync, forever.** A's loop sees `statusCode != 200`, never calls `markOrderAsSynced`, and silently continues; B's `syncOrder` returns `false` and `syncUnsyncedOrders` `break`s. Both surface this to the user only as a generic snackbar/message. No order ever reaches MySQL; inventory is never deducted.

**Error handling & retry.**
- A `sync_service.dart:9-32`: single `try` around the whole loop; on exception returns `false`. **Line 28 `return true;` is reached even when zero orders synced** — a caller cannot distinguish "nothing to do" from "all failed".
- B `sync_service.dart:59-76`: per-order `try/catch` returning `false`; `syncUnsyncedOrders:98-114` **`break`s on the first failure** — one poison order blocks every subsequent order indefinitely (head-of-line blocking, guaranteed permanent stall given the payload bug).
- **Retry logic: none in either.** No scheduler, no timer, no exponential backoff, no max attempts. Retry is only triggered by the user manually tapping the sync icon: A `pos_screen.dart:25-40` (`IconButton` → `SyncService.syncOfflineOrders()`), B `pos_screen.dart:44-48` — and **B's button has an empty callback `onPressed: () {}`**, i.e. it does nothing at all.
- **Connectivity detection is broken in B:** `isServerReachable()` (`sync_service.dart:126-138`) issues `http.head(url)`, but `sync.php` accepts only `POST`/`OPTIONS` and answers `HEAD` with **405** (`sync.php:49-56`), so `isServerReachable()` **always returns `false`**, permanently reporting the server as down.

**Conflict resolution.** **None.** There is no version/`updated_at`/ETag comparison, no last-write-wins policy, no server-side merge. Local rows are write-once and never re-read from the server; no pull/down-sync path exists at all (no `SELECT` from the server anywhere in either client). Two tablets sharing a product ID produce conflicting inventory with no reconciliation.

**Idempotency — and is duplicate submission possible? YES, on several independent paths.**
1. **No idempotency key is transmitted.** A *has* a UUID but sends it as `order_uuid`, a field `sync.php` never reads and no MySQL column stores. B has no UUID at all — it sends its own `order_id`, which `sync.php` also ignores (`:95-107` inserts a fresh autoincrement and never binds the client value).
2. **No uniqueness constraint.** `ddl_core_tables.sql:50-64` defines **no unique key** on `orders` (no `order_uuid`, no `client_id`, no composite), so the database will not reject a replay.
3. **The flag is set only after the response returns.** If the HTTP request reaches the server and commits `$pdo->commit()` (`sync.php:210`) but the response is lost — app killed, tablet sleeps, Wi-Fi drops after the request — then `markOrderAsSynced` never runs and the row stays `is_synced = 0`. The next tap **re-inserts the same order**, duplicating both the order and the inventory deduction.
4. Non-atomic clients make it worse: B's inline checkout calls `insertOrder` **unawaited** (`pos_screen.dart:344`), so a fast double-tap on Confirm can enqueue the same basket twice.
5. **Mid-batch failure semantics differ and are both unsafe.** A: marks each order as it succeeds and continues, so a throw mid-loop leaves earlier orders marked and later ones pending — correct-ish, but the `return true` at `:28` lies about it. B: `break`s, so it marks a prefix and abandons the suffix; because the first order always fails (payload bug), **nothing** is ever marked. Neither wraps the batch in a transaction and neither re-reads the server to detect a partial commit.

## 4. Backend (`sync.php`) audit — 233 lines

**Endpoints/actions.** Exactly one: a flat script at `backend/sync.php`. There is **no router, no action parameter, no versioning**, and no other PHP file exists. It handles only "ingest one order".

**HTTP methods.** `OPTIONS` → 200 + empty exit (`:43-46`). Anything not `POST` → **405** (`:49-56`). No `GET`/`PUT`/`DELETE`; consequently **there is no read/reporting/query endpoint whatsoever**, which is why no reporting module could exist even in principle.

**Input handling & validation.** Reads `php://input`, `json_decode(..., true)` (`:59`); `null` → **400 Invalid JSON** (`:61-68`). Envelope check `empty($input['order'])` → **400** (`:71-78`). Required order fields `['user_id','status','payment_method','items']` via `empty()` → throws (`:88-93`); required item fields `['product_id','quantity']` (`:115-120`). Weaknesses: `empty()` rejects legitimate `0`/`"0"` values; **`status` is never checked against the ENUM** (`'pending','confirmed','preparing','ready','closed','cancelled'`), relying on MySQL strict mode to error out; **`quantity` is never validated as positive or numeric** — `empty(-5)` is `false`, so a **negative quantity passes validation**, producing a negative `$itemTotal` (`:135`), a negative order total (`:136, :154-160`), and a *negative deduction* that **increases** ingredient stock (`:181, :194-195`); `user_id` is not verified to exist or be active (relies on the FK).

**SQL used.** PDO with real prepared statements throughout (`:95-98, :123-125, :139-142, :154-156, :164-169, :193-196`), `PDO::ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES => false` (`:20`), `ERRMODE_EXCEPTION` (`:19`). **No SQL-injection vector found** — all user data is bound. `mysqli` is not used at all; it is PDO-only.

**Authentication/authorization: NONE.** There is no session start, no token/API-key check, no `Authorization` header read, no role check, no rate limiting, no CSRF token, and no device allow-list. The script jumps straight from DB connect to `json_decode`. Combined with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` (`:38`) and a plaintext-HTTP LAN bind, **any host that can reach 192.168.137.1 — including a customer's phone on the hotspot — can inject arbitrary orders, set arbitrary `user_id`, and drain or inflate inventory.** The RBAC/“API-Level RBAC Enforcement” promised in the architecture documents exists nowhere in code.

**Transaction handling.** `beginTransaction` (`:82`), `commit` (`:210`), `rollBack` guarded by `inTransaction()` (`:223-225`). The whole order+items+deduction unit is atomic — this part is genuinely correct. However:
- **Dead concurrency guard:** `:198` `$rowsAffected = $updateIngredient->execute([...])` — `PDOStatement::execute()` returns **`bool`**, not a row count. So `$rowsAffected` is `true`/`false` and the check at `:203` `if ($rowsAffected === 0)` **can never be true**. The intended lost-update detection is inert; the correct call is `->rowCount()`.
- **Query/usage mismatch:** the deduction `SELECT` (`:165-169`) fetches `ri.ingredient_id, ri.quantity_required, i.current_quantity, i.safety_stock` — it does **not** select `i.unit`, yet `:188` interpolates `{$recipe['unit']}` twice. With PHP 8 this raises `Undefined array key "unit"` warnings and emits an error message with an empty unit.
- The stock-sufficiency check (`:184-190`) reads `current_quantity` from the earlier `fetchAll`, then relies on the `WHERE current_quantity >= :deduct_amount` predicate for safety — but because the rowcount check is broken, a genuine concurrent modification is not detected as intended.

**Error responses.** Consistent shape `{success, error, message}`. **Two information-disclosure leaks:** `:29-33` returns `$e->getMessage()` from the PDO connection failure (exposing DSN/host/credentials context) despite the comment "In production, log to file instead of displaying"; `:228-232` returns the raw exception message (`error => $e->getMessage()`), leaking SQL/table/ingredient internals, and also returns `order_id` which may be a rolled-back ID. `Content-Type: application/json` is set (`:37`) but `http_response_code()` is used without `die()` in the catch, and the `success:true` path at `:213` does not explicitly set 200 (PHP defaults to it).

**Idempotency.** **Not idempotent — plain INSERT.** `:95-107` unconditionally inserts a new `orders` row; `:139-150` unconditionally inserts items; `:193-201` unconditionally decrements stock. Replaying an identical payload creates a second order and a second deduction. There is no `INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE`, no unique-key pre-check, and no client-supplied key to dedupe on. **Double submission is fully possible and leaves no way to detect or repair it.**

---

## 5. Excel reporting module — the single most important finding

## **NO. There is no PhpSpreadsheet-based (or any) Excel export code anywhere in the workspace. Zero. Definitively absent.**

Evidence:
1. **Content grep across both Recycle Bin trees** (`PhpSpreadsheet|Spreadsheet|Xlsx|xlsx|Excel|phpoffice`, over `.dart .php .sql .yaml .md .txt .json .html`, excluding generated dirs) → **`NO MATCHES IN ANY SOURCE FILE`**.
2. **Full workspace grep** (earlier, before the path correction) → all 56 `PhpSpreadsheet` matches and all 44 `xlsx` matches were inside `_audit_extracted\*.DOCX` **planning documents**, never in code. Those DOCX hits are aspiration text, e.g. `VENUEVUE SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE...DOCX:26-27` "2.2 Post-Event Export Engine (PhpSpreadsheet Integration) … integrates the open-source PhpSpreadsheet library (v1.28+)", `:31` the "AUTOMATED 4-TAB EXCEL WORKBOOK (.XLSX)" diagram, and `Project Plan 2.0 _1_.DOCX:393` "FR-06 (PhpSpreadsheet Report Engine)".
3. **Exactly one `.php` file exists in the entire tree**: `backend\sync.php`. Full recursive traversal for `*.php` returned only that path. There is no `export.php`, `report.php`, `ExcelExport.php`, `Spreadsheet.php`, or any other backend script.
4. **No PhpSpreadsheet library is installed and no dependency manager exists**: no `composer.json` anywhere in either tree or the workspace, and no `vendor/` directory. PhpSpreadsheet could not be autoloaded even if a script were written.
5. **No `.xlsx`/`.xls` files exist on disk** anywhere in either tree.
6. **No server endpoint that could feed a report exists**: `sync.php` is POST-only ingest (`:49-56`) with no read/aggregate query path, so there is no data-to-Excel pipeline even in skeleton form.
7. The client side has no export either: no `share_plus`, `path_provider`, `csv`, or `excel` package in either `pubspec.yaml`, and no export UI.

**Conclusion: the entire "server-side Excel reporting module using PhpSpreadsheet" — the project's headline post-event deliverable (FR-06, "4-tab Summary/Sales-by-Product/Ingredient-Usage/Restock workbook in ≤10 s") — is 0% implemented.** It exists only as prose in planning documents. This is the largest single gap between declared architecture and delivered code.

---

## 6. Hardcoded values & security issues

**Hardcoded credentials (critical) — `backend\sync.php:10-14`:**
```php
define('DB_HOST', 'localhost');
define('DB_NAME', 'venuevue_db');
define('DB_USER', 'root');
define('DB_PASS', '');
```
MySQL `root` with an **empty password**, committed in source. Classic XAMPP default, but it means the database is unprotected by any credential and the credentials are shipped in the artifact. No `.env`, no config include, no `getenv()`.

**Hardcoded network endpoint (both clients, duplicated):**
- `$RFUPVBI\lib\services\sync_service.dart:7` — `static const String baseUrl = 'http://192.168.137.1/venuevue_api/sync.php';`
- `$RF00UAI\flutevue\lib\sync_service.dart:19` — `static const String _syncEndpoint = 'http://192.168.137.1/venuevue_api/sync.php';`
- Comment at A `:6` — `// Laptop static IP assigned by Windows Mobile Hotspot`. Comment at B `:18` — "Adjust this for your XAMPP server IP address."
A hardcoded RFC1918 address with no build-time override, **plain `http://` (no TLS)**, so all order and credential-adjacent traffic is cleartext on a shared hotspot. `192.168.137.1` also matches the architecture docs (`VENUEVUE SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE...DOCX:19`, "Host Laptop Workstation (192.168.137.1)").

**Missing authentication/authorization (critical).** `sync.php` has **no** auth of any kind — see §4. No API key, session, JWT, HMAC, or RBAC. Every architectural promise of "API-Level RBAC Enforcement" / "RBAC Security & Session Validator" (`VENUEVUE SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE...DOCX:19, 23`) is unimplemented. The Flutter clients send no credential either (A `sync_service.dart:17` and B `sync_service.dart:62` set only `{'Content-Type': 'application/json'}`).

**Permissive CORS — `sync.php:38`:** `header('Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *');` — allows any origin to drive the ingest endpoint from a browser context.

**Information disclosure via exception messages — `sync.php:32` and `:230`:**
```php
'message' => $e->getMessage()      // :32 (DB connection failure)
'error'   => $e->getMessage(),     // :230 (any processing error, incl. SQL/table internals)
```

**PDO vs mysqli.** **PDO exclusively**, correctly configured: `mysql:` DSN (`:17`), `ATTR_ERRMODE => ERRMODE_EXCEPTION` (`:19`), `ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES => false` (`:20`) — so real server-side prepares. **No `mysqli` usage anywhere.** `PDO::ATTR_STRINGIFY_FETCHES`/persistent connections are not set (fine).

**SQL injection risk: NONE found.** All dynamic values go through bound placeholders (`:100-107, :144-150, :157-160, :175, :198-201`). The two string interpolations are not user-controlled SQL — `:91` `"Missing required order field: $field"` interpolates only the hardcoded array element, and `:130` interpolates a cast integer. The file's own header claim (`:5` "Uses prepared statements to prevent SQL injection") holds. **This is the one security control the backend gets right.**

**Plaintext anything.** (a) MySQL root password is empty/plaintext in source (`:13`). (b) All client↔server traffic is unauthenticated cleartext HTTP. (c) No password hashing is implemented client-side or server-side — there is **no login code in either Flutter app at all**, so the `users.password_hash` column (`ddl_core_tables.sql:4`) is never written or verified; `user_id` is a hardcoded literal (`pos_screen.dart:331` and `checkout_dialog.dart:47` both use `userId: 1`), meaning **every order is attributed to whichever user happens to be ID 1** regardless of who is logged in. (d) SQLite local databases are unencrypted (no SQLCipher).

**Other hardcoded/unsafe values.** A `checkout_dialog.dart:66` `'T1-${const Uuid().v4().substring(0, 6)}'` — truncating a v4 UUID to 6 hex chars yields only ~16.7 M values, a meaningful collision risk with **no unique index** to catch it (`database_helper.dart:31`). B `checkout_dialog.dart:42-46` derives its ID from `'${DateTime.now().millisecondsSinceEpoch}'.hashCode.abs()` — collision-prone and not a UUID, while B's `pos_screen.dart:330` uses the literal `orderId: 0`.

## 8. Concrete technical risks (ranked)

1. **Order sync is 100% non-functional — payload shape never matches the backend.** `sync_service.dart:18` (A) / `sync_service.dart:63` (B) post a flat map, but `sync.php:71` requires a nested `$input['order']` array → HTTP 400 on every request; and both omit the `items` array that `sync.php:88/114` requires. *Remediation:* wrap the payload as `{"order": {..., "items": [...]}}` and include line items from `local_order_items` / `order_items`.

2. **No idempotency anywhere → duplicate orders and duplicate stock deductions are guaranteed.** `sync.php:95-107` unconditionally INSERTs, `ddl_core_tables.sql:50-64` has no unique key, and clients mark synced only after the response returns (`sync_service.dart:24` A, `:104` B), so a lost response replays the order. *Remediation:* add `orders.client_order_uuid CHAR(36) NOT NULL UNIQUE`, send it from the client, and use `INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE` / return the existing order id.

3. **Backend is completely unauthenticated on a shared hotspot with wildcard CORS.** `sync.php` has no auth code at all; `sync.php:38` sets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`. Any device that joins the hotspot can create orders, set arbitrary `user_id`, and manipulate inventory. *Remediation:* require a per-device bearer token with a constant-time compare, and replace `*` with an explicit origin allow-list.

4. **MySQL root with an empty password hardcoded in source.** `sync.php:10-14` (`DB_USER 'root'`, `DB_PASS ''`). *Remediation:* move credentials to a git-ignored config/`.env` read via `getenv()`, and create a least-privilege `venuevue` DB user.

5. **Exception messages leak database/SQL internals.** `sync.php:32` and `sync.php:230` return `$e->getMessage()` to the client. *Remediation:* log server-side, return only a generic error code/message.

6. **Negative `quantity` passes validation and inflates inventory.** `sync.php:115-120` uses `empty()` (which accepts `-5`), then `:135-136` computes negative totals and `:181/194-195` performs a *negative* deduction that increases `current_quantity`. *Remediation:* validate `is_numeric($item['quantity']) && (int)$item['quantity'] > 0` (and cap at a sane maximum) before use.

7. **Broken concurrency guard is dead code.** `sync.php:198` assigns `PDOStatement::execute()` (a `bool`) to `$rowsAffected`, so `if ($rowsAffected === 0)` at `:203` can never fire; lost updates on concurrent deductions go undetected. *Remediation:* use `$updateIngredient->rowCount()` and/or add `FOR UPDATE` locking on the `ingredients` row.

8. **Runtime-fatal missing provider registration in codebase B.** `flutevue\lib\main.dart:5-7` has no `MultiProvider`, but `pos_screen.dart:13/104` and `checkout_dialog.dart:97` call `Provider.of<CartProvider>`/`context.watch<CartProvider>`; `flutter analyze` confirms `warning - Unused import: '../provider/cart_provider.dart' - lib/main.dart:2:8`. B crashes with `ProviderNotFoundException` on launch. *Remediation:* wrap `VenueVueApp` in `ChangeNotifierProvider(create: (_) => CartProvider())` as codebase A does at `main.dart:10-13`.

9. **B's checkout writes order items with `order_id = 0`, orphaning every line item, and never awaits the writes.** `pos_screen.dart:330` sets `orderId: 0`; `:344` and `:355` call `insertOrder`/`insertOrderItem` **without `await`**; the generated rowid is discarded. Items are therefore attached to a non-existent order, and a double-tap can enqueue duplicates. *Remediation:* `await` `insertOrder`, capture the returned rowid, use it as `order_id` for items, and wrap both in one transaction.

10. **`checkout_dialog.dart` in B (191 lines) is dead code — duplicate, divergent checkout logic.** It is never imported (verified by grep: only self-references), while `pos_screen.dart:277` reimplements checkout inline. The two disagree on validation (dead copy validates `cash < totalAmount` at `:33`; live copy does not) and on ID generation (`checkout_dialog.dart:46` hashed ms-timestamp vs `pos_screen.dart:330` literal `0`). *Remediation:* delete `pos_screen.dart:277-371` and use the real `CheckoutDialog`.

11. **Head-of-line blocking in B's sync loop permanently stalls the queue.** `sync_service.dart:106-113` `break`s on the first failure; combined with risk #1 (first order always fails), no order is ever synced. *Remediation:* `continue` on failure with a per-order attempt counter and backoff, and surface a durable "needs attention" state.

12. **`isServerReachable()` always returns false.** `sync_service.dart:129/180` uses `http.head`, but `sync.php:49-56` answers non-POST with 405. *Remediation:* probe with a `POST` of an empty/health payload against an explicit `/health` action, or accept `HEAD`/`GET` in the backend.

13. **SQLite foreign keys are declared but never enforced.** Neither `database_helper.dart` sets `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` (grepped: absent in both), so B's `order_items` FK (`database_helper.dart:73`) is inert and orphan rows are already being created (risk #9). *Remediation:* add `onConfigure: (db) => db.execute('PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON')` to `openDatabase`.

14. **`A` returns `true` from sync even when every order failed.** `sync_service.dart:28` `return true;` after the loop, regardless of per-order outcomes. *Remediation:* return a result object with `total`, `synced`, `failed` counts and drive the UI from it.

15. **Weak, colliding client order identifiers.** A truncates a UUID to 6 hex chars (`checkout_dialog.dart:66`); B uses a hashed millisecond timestamp (`checkout_dialog.dart:42-46`) or the literal `0` (`pos_screen.dart:330`); SQLite has no unique index on either. *Remediation:* store and transmit a full `Uuid().v4()` with a `UNIQUE` index, and use it as the server idempotency key.

16. **`sync.php:188` reads an unselected column.** The deduction query (`:165-169`) omits `i.unit`, so `{$recipe['unit']}` raises `Undefined array key "unit"` warnings and produces a malformed error message. *Remediation:* add `i.unit` to the SELECT.

17. **A's post-checkout success dialog uses a popped route's `BuildContext`.** `flutter analyze` flags `checkout_dialog.dart:97:33` and `:101:30` (`use_build_context_synchronously`) because `Navigator.pop(context)` at `:97` precedes `showDialog(context: context)` at `:100`. The confirmation may fail to display. *Remediation:* show the success dialog from the parent screen's context (or a `ScaffoldMessenger`), not the dismissed dialog's.

18. **Hardcoded endpoint prevents deployment to any other host.** `sync_service.dart:7` (A) / `:19` (B) pin `http://192.168.137.1/...` with no override, no environment config, and plain cleartext HTTP. *Remediation:* inject the base URL via `--dart-define`/env config and terminate behind HTTPS or use a pinned local certificate.

19. **No retry, backoff, or durable failure state; sync is purely manual.** Retry depends on a user tap — and in B that tap is a no-op (`pos_screen.dart:44-48`, `onPressed: () {}`). *Remediation:* add a `sync_attempts`/`last_error` column, a background retry with exponential backoff, and reconnect-triggered sync.

20. **`INVENTORY_TRANSACTIONS` and `AUDIT_LOGS` are missing from the schema.** `ddl_core_tables.sql` has only 6 tables, yet `sync.php:193-201` mutates stock in place with no movement log. There is **no audit trail** for who sold, voided, or adjusted what — a serious control gap for a cash-handling POS. *Remediation:* add `inventory_transactions` (ingredient_id, delta, reason, order_id, user_id, created_at) and an append-only `audit_logs` table, and write to both inside the existing transaction.

**Supporting evidence files:** `$RF00UAI\backend\sync.php`, `$RF00UAI\sql\ddl_core_tables.sql`, `$RF00UAI\flutevue\sync_service.dart`, `$RF00UAI\flutevue\pos_screen.dart`, `$RF00UAI\flutevue\checkout_dialog.dart`, `$RF00UAI\flutevue\database_helper.dart`, `$RF00UAI\flutevue\models\order_model.dart`, `$RF00UAI\flutevue\issues.txt`, `$RFUPVBI\lib\services\sync_service.dart`, `$RFUPVBI\lib\services\database_helper.dart`, `$RFUPVBI\lib\screens\checkout_dialog.dart`, `$RFUPVBI\lib\screens\pos_screen.dart`, `$RFUPVBI\lib\providers\cart_provider.dart`.

**Scope note / limitation:** I did not modify any file. I ran `flutter analyze --no-pub` read-only on both projects; no build, no `pub get`, no network write. I did not test `sync.php` against a live MySQL/XAMPP instance, so the runtime behaviour claims in §3/§4 are from static reading of the exact code paths (line references given) rather than an executed end-to-end test."}
